title: Automated VPC probe playbook for token-throughput and adaptive SLOs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a reproducible, Terraform-deployable probe suite and operational playbook for VPC/private deployments focused on token throughput, latency tails, error rates, and saturation signals. The goal is to provide deterministic SLO probes that detect regressions in throughput and latency under realistic KV-cache and batching configurations, integrate with autoscaling rules and upgrade hooks, and surface actionable alerts with runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module 'vpc_probe' deploys probes as namespaced Deployment + Service + ServiceMonitor and creates Alertmanager rules via upstream alerting module

Synthetic token-throughput probe generates representative gRPC/text requests exercising KV cache hits and misses; Prometheus metrics exported: probe_request_duration_seconds_bucket, probe_errors_total, probe_tokens_processed_total
SLOs expressed as Prometheus recording rules: p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, error_rate_pct, token_throughput_per_gpu; alerts fire when sustained breach for configured evaluation window
Runbook created and linked for each alert with automated remediation: graceful throttling, scale-up policy, temporary fallback to smaller compatible model, and automatic slack pager escalation
Probe lifecycle hooks included in Terraform module: pre-upgrade sensitivity reduction and post-upgrade verification step that re-enables standard thresholds
End-to-end tests in CI validate probe deployment, metric emission, alert rule compilation, and a simulated saturation event triggers expected autoscaling path

decisions: Probes will run as in-cluster deployment in the customer's VPC by default (sidecar option is available but not defaulted) to avoid cross-VPC latency noise
Token throughput SLI is defined as tokens_processed_total per GPU per minute averaged over 5m and 1h windows — we will derive per-AZ normalization factors at onboarding
Latency SLOs: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 400ms for text-generation endpoints under 1024 context with KV-cache enabled; these are starting defaults and marked configurable per-customer
Error-rate SLO: 0.05% 5m error rate target for production traffic; alerts at 0.2% sustained over 10m

During platform upgrades we reduce probe sensitivity (increase thresholds) to avoid noisy alerts and use a post-upgrade verification probe runbook to ensure feature parity before re-enabling stricter SLOs
implementation_notes: Create a small Go probe binary that replays prompt templates with variable token lengths and optional KV cache warm/cold phases; binary exposes Prometheus metrics and a /healthz endpoint
Metrics to emit: probe_request_duration_seconds (histogram), probe_errors_total (counter), probe_tokens_processed_total (counter), probe_concurrency_gauge
Prometheus recording rules: derive p95/p99 from histogram; calculate error_rate = increase(probe_errors_total[5m]) / increase(probe_requests_total[5m]) * 100
Token saturation detection: compare tokens_processed_total against a derived capacity model (tokens_per_gpu_capacity) and alert on sustained >85% utilization for 10m
Terraform module should accept 'sensitivity_profile' (low/standard/strict) that maps to alert thresholds and evaluation windows so we can set customer- or upgrade-specific profiles
Expose an output from IaC: probe_id, service_endpoint, service_account; ensure secrets minimal and rotate-friendly; follow private-deployments security checklist
Integrate with autoscaler: alert -> webhook -> autoscale policy that can increase replica target, add GPUs, or route % traffic to dedicated endpoints depending on entitlement
